newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria bases oil income 1996-99 on $15-$17 barrel.
newsitem.headline: Algeria bases oil income 1996-99 on $15-$17 barrel.

text.p: Algeria has based forecasts of oil income at between $15 and $17 a barrel during the period 1996 to 1999, according to a report from the Algerian presidency obtained by Reuters.

The report, the basis of debate on the economy in Algiers last week, said that at $15 a barrel, Algeria's income for that period would be around $41.2 billion. At $17, the North African OPEC member would earn around $44.8 billion.
Algeria, traditionally cautious in its forecasts, estimated income for 1995 on an average price of $16.27 per barrel, while the actual price was $17.9 a barrel.
In the first half of 1996, average income was $22 a barrel, against estimates in its 1996 calendar year budget of $16.5 a barrel.
